title: Lina's Warm Buns
markdown:
The kitchen smelled warm and sweet. Lina put her hot cross buns on the windowsill. They were for the village fair. Moss the hedgehog watched, his nose twitching.

“They look wonderful, Lina!” Auntie June said. “So lovely and warm!”

But Lina sighed. She touched a bun. The cozy warmth was fading. Moss nudged a bun. “They’re not as warm,” he whispered. This was a problem for the fair.

Lina frowned. She looked at the air above the buns. It shimmered a little. The warmth was floating away, like a gentle river.

“Let’s try something!” Lina said. She grabbed a soft tea towel. “If the warm is drifting away,” she explained to Moss, “we can wrap it up like a cozy blanket.” She draped the tea towel over the buns.

They waited. Moss nudged a bun under the towel. “It’s still warm!” he chirped. Lina also put buns on a wire rack. This helped too! The heat didn’t rush away so fast.

“Look!” Lina clapped her hands. “The warmth stays longer when we help it!” Auntie June beamed. “Heat likes to move from where there’s lots of it to where there’s less. Wrapping them keeps them snug.”

With their buns wrapped warmly, Lina, Moss, and Auntie June walked to the fair. The villagers loved the buns. “Wonderfully warm!” said Mrs. Gable.

As they sold their last bun, Lina looked at Moss. A curious sparkle lit up her eyes. “I wonder,” she said, “what other journeys heat takes?”
characters: Lina the patient inventor, Moss the hedgehog, Auntie June
